findings.current: On top of a high sand dune, The Prophet spotted evacuation vehicles moving through a thick cloud of dust. His eyes lit up.
findings.defect: The draft places the Prophet on the dune. The source places the moving vehicles there and says they are kicking up the dust.
findings.rationale: 높은 모래 언덕 위 describes where the vehicles are moving; 일으키며 makes them the cause of the dust cloud.
findings.replacement: The Prophet’s eyes lit up as he spotted transport vehicles moving along a high sand dune, kicking up a thick cloud of dust.
findings.source: 높은 모래 언덕 위, 자욱한 먼지구름을 일으키며 움직이는 후송 차량들을 확인한 선지자는 눈을 빛냈다.

findings.current: People had found out that he’d missed the ceremony twice in a row—first the Leviathan incident, and now the launch ceremony.
findings.defect: The draft turns two different absences into two missed ceremonies.
findings.rationale: The Leviathan incident was the first occasion; only the second was a ceremony.
findings.replacement: People had found out that he’d failed to show up twice in a row: first during the Leviathan incident, then at the launch ceremony.
findings.source: 그가 레비아탄 사태에 이어, 발족식까지 2연속 불참했다는 사실이 알려졌기 때문이었다.

findings.current: └ He’s really good at Swift Retreat.
findings.defect: “Retreat” changes the joke from repeatedly failing to show up to fleeing a fight.
findings.rationale: 질풍불참 substitutes 불참, nonattendance, into the preceding 질풍참 technique name.

findings.current: └ ;;;; These bastards are jumping straight into Jin-construction the second they get a chance to kill him.
findings.defect: The draft makes 킬각 a literal chance to kill Jin, although the comment is about an opening to claim him as Chinese.
findings.rationale: The preceding comment claims Jin’s family originated in China; 킬각 is figurative internet slang for a timely opening, not a threat to kill him.
findings.replacement: └ ;;;; The second they see an opening, these bastards launch straight into their Jin-is-Chinese campaign.
findings.source: └ ;;;;이 새끼들 킬각 나오자마자 바로 진북공정 들어오네.

findings.current: the Prime Minister was broadcasting the fact that Japan’s head of state was a lunatic through the loudspeaker that was the media.
findings.defect: “Head of state” assigns the prime minister an office the source does not; 국가 지도자 means national leader.
findings.rationale: The sentence mocks the prime minister for publicly exposing his own unfitness, without identifying him as head of state.
findings.replacement: the Prime Minister was using the media as a loudspeaker to announce, without a hint of restraint, that Japan’s leader was a lunatic.
findings.source: 총리는 언론이라는 확성기에 대고 일본의 국가 지도자가 미친놈이라는 사실을 가감 없이 밝히고 있다.

summary: Several localized errors alter the Prophet’s position, Yamamoto’s record of absences, and an internet joke.
